Hence open $\Rightarrow$ generalizing; universally open $\Rightarrow$ universally generalizing. Generalizing is stable under composition (universally generalizing also under base change), and weaker than open.
Example: $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\to X$, $\eta$ a maximal point: generalizing, not open in general (e.g. for the affine line).
Open versus generalizing
Theorem. $f$ locally of finite presentation: $f$ open $\iff$ $f$ generalizing; hence universally open $\iff$ universally generalizing.

Idea: the image of an open set is stable under generalization; the image of a scheme of finite presentation is constructible (finite union of locally closed sets if noetherian), and a constructible set stable under generalization is open (EGA I, constructible subsets).
Reduce to $Y$ noetherian by passage to the limit.

Flatness
$A$ a ring, $M$ an $A$-module. Flat: $N\mapsto M\otimes_AN$ is exact. Faithfully flat: flat and $T=M\otimes_A-$ faithful, i.e. $M\otimes N=0\Rightarrow N=0$.
M\ \text{faithfully flat}\iff\bigl(u\ \text{injective (surjective, bijective)}\iff T(u)=M\otimes u\ \text{injective (surjective, bijective)}\bigr)
N'\to N\to N''\ \text{exact}\iff T(N')\to T(N)\to T(N'')\ \text{exact}
For an $A$-algebra $B$: flat means base change $N\mapsto N_B$ is exact; faithfully flat means exact and faithful.
Criterion for faithful flatness
$M$ is faithfully flat iff $M$ is flat and
M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak m)=M/\mathfrak mM\neq0\quad\text{for every maximal ideal }\mathfrak m\subset A

Algebra $B$: faithfully flat $\iff$ flat and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ surjective $\iff$ the fibres over maximal ideals are non-empty.
$A\to B$ a local homomorphism of local rings: flat $\Rightarrow$ faithfully flat, since $B/\mathfrak mB\neq0$ ($\mathfrak mB\subset\mathfrak m_B$).
Flatness is stable under localization: $B$ flat over $A$ $\Rightarrow$ $B[T^{-1}]$ flat over $A[S^{-1}]$; so local rings of $B$ are flat over local rings of $A$.
Hence: $A\to B$ flat $\Rightarrow$ $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ generalizing ($\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ local, flat, faithfully flat).
Flatness for sheaves and schemes

$\mathcal M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module is flat iff all stalks $\mathcal M_x$ are flat; for $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathcal M=\tilde M$ flat $\iff$ $M_{\mathfrak p}$ flat over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ $\iff$ $M$ flat.
$f\colon X\to Y$ ringed spaces, $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$: $\mathcal M$ is flat over $Y$ if $\mathcal M_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$.
Flat morphism: $\mathcal O_X$ flat over $Y$; for affines, $B$ flat over $A$; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Flat $\Rightarrow$ generalizing.
Flat morphisms are stable under composition and base change ($M$ flat over $A$ $\Rightarrow$ $M'=M\otimes_AA'$ flat over $A'$, since $M'\otimes_{A'}N'=M\otimes_AN'$).
Faithfully flat morphism: flat and surjective; stable under composition and base change.
f\ \text{faithfully flat}\iff f^*\colon\mathrm{Mod}(Y)\to\mathrm{Mod}(X)\ \text{exact and faithful}
If $f^*M=0$: $(f^*M)_x=M_y\otimes\mathcal O_{X,x}=0$ for all $x$, and every $y$ has an $x$ above it, so $M=0$.
Irreducible components under flat morphisms
$f\colon X\to Y$ flat: every irreducible component of $X$ dominates an irreducible component of $Y$.
